verdictLine: Medium risk · needs work · 1 blocker · 7 gaps

intent.stated: Add offering fields to the catalog, two new output skills, restructured deck/one-pager/microsite methods, a battlecard built from Octave's own competitor data, ads copy guidance, abm cohort plans, lookalike prospecting, and data schemas from #76.

actual.text: Implements each listed item as skill prose, catalog entries and JSON schemas. It also adds a fixed qualification pass score and Octave tool lists to abm and prospector.

attention.title: Cohort plans have no matching data shape
attention.detail: abm now writes cohort plans, but its new output schema only fits a single-account plan. It requires `accountName` and stakeholders, and has no place for cohort members, tiers or plays per tier. The cohort method forbids naming contacts for individual accounts. A host that asks a cohort run for data will get an invented account, or rows that fail the schema.

attention.title: Six changelogs put the new release last
attention.detail: Every other changelog lists the newest release first. For ads, battlecard-doc, deck, microsite, one-pager and win-loss-report, the new entry was added after 1.0.0 instead. Any reader that takes the first entry as the latest will show stale release notes for these six skills.

attention.title: Deal card order conflicts with section template
attention.detail: battlecard-doc's method now sets a nine-part deal card in order of weight. The unchanged sections reference still sets a different layout: strengths/weaknesses grids, watch-outs, trap questions and Our Pitch. Win rates now come from `get_entity` includeUsage and competitive insights, but later in the same file they come from `get_entity_outcome_stats`.

attention.title: Fixed pass score of 7 for qualification
attention.detail: prospector and abm now treat a score of 7 out of 10 as qualified. The same prospector method says to use the configured qualification, and that unknown is not false. A workspace whose agent passes at a different score, or a candidate with unanswered questions, gets labeled not qualified. The description doesn't mention this rule.

attention.title: Lookalike route skips saved qualification agents
attention.detail: The prospector method says to prefer the workspace's saved qualification agent (`run_qualify_company_agent`) and fall back to `qualify_company`. The new lookalike route and the skill entry tell the model to run `qualify_company` and `qualify_person` on every candidate. That conflicts with the description's 'the workspace's own qualification'.

attention.title: New catalog fields are never validated
attention.detail: The validator checks only that each skill has a catalog key. A typo in a `kind`, pillar, `outputs` id or `about` word would ship unnoticed. The docs list the allowed ids, and the current values all match them.

attention.title: Seven changed skills not run end to end
attention.detail: The description says deck, one-pager, microsite, battlecard-doc, ads, abm and prospector weren't run to completion after their change. These are the riskiest behavior changes: prospector's new default route, abm cohort plans, and battlecard-doc's new sources. No automated test covers skill prose.

attention.title: ads 1.3.0 changelog entry appended last
attention.detail: If the catalog sync reads the first changelog entry as the latest release, ads 1.3.0 shows the 1.2.1 notes. The 1.3.0 entry sits after 1.0.0, but every other skill lists newest first. validate() never compares version with the changelog, so CI passes and both main workflows publish it. Ask how octave-app orders or picks entries, and move this one to the top.

overview.oneLine: Adds offering metadata to every catalog entry, two new output skills, abm cohort plans, lookalike-first prospecting, a sourced battlecard, and data schemas for five skills.
overview.riskLine: All changes are skill prose and JSON, but default behavior shifts for several customer-facing skills that weren't rerun, and another repo consumes the new fields and schemas.
overview.plain: Once the paired octave-app change ships, Octave can show each skill by an everyday name and group it by sales area. Users get long-form document and magazine skills. Account planning can cover a whole segment, and prospecting starts from companies like recent wins.

terms.meaning: A job gathers evidence and decides what to say; an output only shapes how a deck, page or document looks and reads.
The go-to-market area a skill is filed under, such as outbound or deal execution, used to group skills in the app.
Companies and buyers that resemble accounts the team has already won, used as a starting list of prospects.
